title: MZ Hello, very new, and with many questions.

posts.author: NiNoZaPo
posts.body:
Hello, very new to the to the RPG Maker circle.
Been mostly lurking thread to threat, trying to get the right information I need for my game (which is stuck on paper. Drew a little doodle of it too lol)
Anyways, questions I have in mind, and please go easy on me since I'm still a scrub at all of this:
-Is there a way, or at least plugins, I can use well time attacks in battle?
-Personally, I don't want to create a full on mapping system for me game, more like a POV like view. Kinda like in ace attorney where player points and click at a location/event, and stuff happens. Is that possible?
-Is there a way I can mess with armor/weapons weights that could effect gameplay? Like if a sword is too heavy for a party member, there's chances of getting a hit has a 20/80 chance of making it. Something like that.
-And, since I drew this little doodle, I'm not that good with Pixel art. I know RPG Maker can do line art type of stuff, though, I'm struggling to find the right videos to do so.
-Last one,  I tend to go to  itch io for the  latest plug-ins, but if you guys know any other sites (or better yet, maybe knows who may take commissions to do a plug  in) might send me a link.
Again, new here, most likely this is the wrong place to even post my rambling, like I said though, I'm new

posts.author: Gamera
posts.body:
I can't speak for the programming side of things, but on general digital raster illustrations (regular) and pixel art, you should just be able to import images with a transparent .png (make sure it's all lowercase) background into the image folders.
I think people like using pixel art since it's a bit easier to modify since you can do things like recolor & select easier without the transparent pixels.  Plus, it makes shapes clearer at smaller sizes.
You can always try for an illustrative style like so (hope you don't mind the pixel over):
This example is fast and a little sloppy, but you can incorporate anti-aliasing by hand to smooth some of the lineart & shade like a cell shaded picture [ISPOILER](ribbit)[/ISPOILER].
Spoiler:
examples of more illustrative pixel art
Pokemon
Marvel vs Capcom
For a more sketchy or painterly style, going for regular images with transparent pixels is easier.  If you'd like to learn pixel art, there's plenty of
beginner's tutorials out there
, but go for the style you want or is easiest for you.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
SGHarlekin said:
For point and click gameplay, you'll likely want to use what we call "Parallax mapping".
Click to expand...
The more typical solution is to use a plugin to activate common events when clicking on images shown via Show Image. MZ has a ButtonPicture plugin that's included by default in every new project.
If you want something fancier, this one includes limiting the clickable area to non-transparent sections:
[CGMZ] Clickable Pictures for RPG Maker MZ by Casper Gaming
Easily create picture based UI direct in editor
casper-gaming.itch.io

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
both approaches described above are valid, the main difference is if you want an (usually oversized) character going to the event in each picture-based room or not.
the parallax approach makes the character handling easier, if you do not want that then the button pictures method is easier.
